title: Sky owes offboarded vault users advance notice because forced unwinding harms them even when the liquidation penalty is zero
content:
A.3.7.1.5.1 is unusually candid for a protocol rulebook. It records that "there have been several instances where users entered official Sky forums/chats to understand why they had been suddenly liquidated, despite historically comfortable collateralization ratios," cites the forum post documenting it, and concludes: "This is, understandably, a poor user experience."

It then rejects the obvious defence that zeroing the liquidation penalty makes offboarding harmless: "Even with liquidation penalties set to 0%, the forced unwinding of levered positions conceivably can result in user losses, as well as potentially taxable events." The harm is in the forced timing, not the fee — a user liquidated at a moment they did not choose realizes losses and, in many jurisdictions, a taxable disposal they had not planned.

This converts offboarding from a purely technical parameter change into an obligation with a communications component. The stated objective is "to minimize the number of users who are unaware of the offboarding prior to getting their positions liquidated," explicitly "on a best-effort basis" — a duty of effort, not of outcome.

A.3.7.1.5.1.1's four goals show the balance being struck: codify good-faith communication, keep the process light enough for contributors to actually follow, minimize unaware users, and preserve a bypass for security or solvency emergencies. The design concedes that a notice regime nobody follows protects no one, and that in a genuine emergency user notice cannot outrank solvency.
description: The Atlas cites real cases of users liquidated despite comfortable ratios, and concedes that unwinding levered positions can cause losses and taxable events regardless of penalty settings.
